doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Birth in Atlantic City, kidnap threat and move to New York
summary: Most recounts a kidnap threat against the twins that sent the family to New York when he was four, and his father's candy store and moonshining.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You know you and your brother, your family went back and forth between New York and Atlantic City.

That’s right. Well I was born in Atlantic City, but there’s some story, I don’t know if my brother told you but someone put a little letter in the box, “We’d like to kidnap one of your twins.” And I’m a twin. I have a twin sister. They said if you don’t hand over a certain amount of money, ten thousand or whatever it was at the time. And so —
No I’m not making this up.

So they were in Atlantic City my folks, so they couldn’t find out who did it. I guess they had the FBI out. And they got scared and they said let’s move out of here, you know someone put a threat in. I don’t know if it was a family member or whether outside the family, but that’s what — my father had a little grocery business or something. So we moved to New York when I was four, so I really consider myself a New Yorker. So I was living there until about 1960, and I was born in 1930.
Wow, I hadn’t heard that story before. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
Yeah, he probably didn’t mention that, but that’s one of the things, when you mentioned Atlantic City, I remember there was a piano in Atlantic City. I think we had an upstairs and a downstairs.
So that’s your memory of really your birthplace.
You said your father was a grocer? He had a grocery store?
He had a candy store or something, yeah. And I think he did some, well during the depression I hear he did some moonshining.
Cool. A little family history there.
I mean how much candy can you actually sell?
